scope: Corollary 9.1 (The hard maximal operator) of the manuscript “Annular variation of the triangular Hilbert transform at the symmetric point” (preprints/Annular-variation-of-the-triangular-Hilbert-transform-at-the-symmetric-point-October-5-2026/annular-variation.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 082 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 f5857c58037fa528), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 32-33. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For complex F, G ∈ L3(R2), define B∗(F, G)(x, y) = sup 0<ε<R<∞ |Bε,R(F, G)(x, y)| 32 on the common full-measure set of Lemma 2.1, and set it to zero elsewhere. This function is measurable, and there is an absolute constant CM such that ∥B∗(F, G)∥p ≤ CM ∥F∥3∥G∥3. (9.1) The supremum includes both finite hard truncation endpoints. Moreover, B∗ is a continuous map from L3(R2) × L3(R2) to Lp(R2) and is the unique continuous extension of its values on compactly supported smooth pairs.
